# Interface token and nominal array context

Owned Java declarations bind a single CharSequence-bounded method formal through Class<T> while preserving an independent File and the original fixed-arity CharSequence[] varargs argument. The provider declares IOException and keeps its original bound cast. No filesystem operation is performed.

Four frozen callers compare 96 cases twice against rebuilt source and dependency-provider recovery: null context/token/array, empty and covariant arrays, identity and partial writes, exact checked/runtime/Error failures, provider casts and later caller casts. Six incorrect programs and six Code-preserving Signature controls verify that the observer detects changed behavior and the binder rejects unproved contracts.

The `--instance-member` variant retains a public virtual provider with the same
interface-bounded token/result relation and closed IOException declaration.
An opaque Key context, receiver, token and returned reference are observed by
four frozen entry routes over 128 fresh JVM cases twice. A separately compiled
future subclass checks virtual dispatch. Null and mismatched tokens, null
receivers, partial writes, callback configuration changes, exact checked/runtime/
Error failures, provider bound casts and later caller casts remain observable.
Nine wrong programs and seven Code-preserving Signature controls qualify the
observer; all emitted source and original class/method metadata are checked.
